items.h: Week 7 winners and losers: Pollard, Burrow lead the way; Walker III, Purdy struggle
items.s: Tony Pollard, Joe Burrow and Zay Flowers came up big in Week 7, while Brock Purdy, Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker III all had quiet days.

items.h: Zay Flowers excellent in Week 7 loss
items.s: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in a 35-13 loss to the Bengals. Flowers opened the scoring on a 48-yard touchdown in the first quarter. Flowers led the team in all receiving categories, and he will look to do the same in Week 8 against the Bills.

items.h: Stellar numbers in lopsided loss
items.s: Flowers brought in eight of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens' 35-13 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. The standout receiver had a big hand in staking the Ravens to a 13-0 halftime lead, and although Baltimore couldn't muster a single point in the second half, Flowers still finished with team-high reception, receiving yardage and target totals. Flowers also had a game-long 48-yard catch, which qualified as his third touchdown of the season. Flowers has shown excellent chemistry with both Lamar Jackson (ankle) and Tyler Huntley, and reports indicate the fleet-footed receiver is likely to have the former under center for a Week 8 road showdown against the Bills.

items.s: The standout receiver had a big hand in staking the Ravens to a 13-0 halftime lead, and although Baltimore couldn't muster a single point in the second half, Flowers still finished with team-high reception, receiving yardage and target totals. items.h: Why Zay Flowers is on WR1 radar for Week 8 in fantasy football
Zay Flowers has Massive Performance in Loss
items.s: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers posted his best performance of the season against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. He got the fun started early with a 48-yard touchdown in the first quarter. The Bengals' defense had absolutely no answers for Flowers during this game. Flowers hauled in eight of his 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in the loss. The 26-year-old led the team in all receiving categories during this game. Flowers has shown excellent chemistry with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. The expectation is that Lamar Jackson should be back next game for a road matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Flowers should remain a strong WR1 for that game.

items.h: Zay Flowers a Borderline WR1 With Starting QB in Question
items.s: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers has been great so far heading into a Week 7 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. In the five games he has played, he has posted double-digit half-PPR points in each one. The 26-year-old receiver is the clear top target and has been efficient, catching at least 80 percent of his targets, except for last week's loss. With Lamar Jackson missing the last two games but potentially returning this week, his efficiency should return to that 80 percent level while also maintaining his average of 10 targets per game from the last three weeks. Top Bengals cornerback DJ Turner has been a nuisance to opposing WR1s this season, but fantasy managers shouldn't be…

items.h: Zay Flowers Drawing Plenty of Targets in Baltimore
items.s: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers is off to a strong start to the season, even though he missed a game with an injury and has been without QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) for his last two contests. Flowers is up to 42 targets in his five games this year and has 32 receptions for 471 yards and two touchdowns. He has racked up over 50 yards per game in every game this season and has averaged 10 targets per game over his last three contests. So far this season, Flowers has the fourth-highest target share in the NFL this season, behind only studs Jaxon Smith-Njigba, DeVonta Smith, and Puka Nacua. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is finding ways to get Flowers plenty of chances to make…

items.h: Six catches in Week 6 loss
items.s: Flowers brought in six of 11 targets for 66 yards and rushed once for one yard in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Flowers set the pace for the Ravens in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, displaying solid chemistry with Tyler Huntley once again. The speedy wideout has no fewer than five catches and 53 receiving yards in any game this season, and he's recorded a 14-118-0 line over the last two games alone with Huntley under center. Flowers will remain a must-play wideout regardless of who's helming the Ravens offense in a Week 7 home matchup against the division-rival Bengals next Sunday.

items.h: Zay Flowers logs season-high 11 targets in Week 6
items.s: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers caught six passes for 66 yards on a season-high 11 targets in Week 6 against the Cleveland Browns. Flowers' weekly floor has been impressive this season, recording at least 50 yards in every contest this season. It was his second game with double-digit targets in a concentrated passing attack that has been successful this season. When Lamar Jackson returns, Flowers has a higher ceiling, having failed to reach the end zone in the last two weeks.

items.h: Zay Flowers Looks to Continue his WR1 Campaign in Week 6
items.s: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (toe) surprised some managers this week with a different injury designation than the hamstring and foot injuries he carried between Weeks 2 and 5. Still, he lacks a questionable tag as the team heads to Cleveland to face the Browns in Week 6. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will start again this weekend while Lamar Jackson (ankle) continues to heal, but Flowers' usage between quarterbacks was largely similar. In Week 5, Flowers caught eight of his nine targets for 53 yards and sustained a 28% target share, 27% air yards share, and 97% route participation, all consistent with his 2025 and 2026 season averages. The only troubling metric was…

items.h: Zay Flowers (toe) good to go for Sunday
items.s: Zay Flowers (toe) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns. Baltimore's star wide receiver will be available to play on Sunday, despite still dealing with a minor toe injury of some kind. Fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to start him this week, although his ceiling will be considerably lower than usual with QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) set to be sidelined for another week.

items.h: Cleared to play
items.s: Flowers (toe) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game at Cleveland. The Ravens added Flowers to their injury report Thursday as a limited participant, and while he remained limited Friday, his game availability isn't in doubt. Tyler Huntley is making another start at quarterback with Lamar Jackson (ankle) ruled out again.

items.h: Flowers (toe) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game at Cleveland.
items.s: The Ravens added Flowers to their injury report Thursday as a limited participant, and while he remained limited Friday, his game availability isn't in doubt. Tyler Huntley is making another start at quarterback with Lamar Jackson (ankle) ruled out again.

items.h: Flowers (toe) is practicing Friday after being added to the injury report Thursday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Flowers was a limited participant Thursday due to the toe injury, and it apparently isn't serious enough to keep him off the field at Friday's practice. His level of participation and any game designation on the Ravens' final injury report should provide more clarity.

items.h: Flowers (toe) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
items.s: Flowers has been no stranger to the injury report this season, having missed a game due to a hamstring injury in Week 2 while also dealing with a foot injury. It's unclear if this latest toe injury is related to his previous foot issue, through which Flowers played in the Week 5 win over Atlanta. Flowers caught eight passes for 53 yards from backup QB Tyler Huntley in that game, and Huntley could be under center again for Sunday's game against the Browns, as Lamar Jackson (ankle) has yet to return to practice. Flowers' practice participation will bear monitoring Friday, though he could still…

items.h: Flowers (foot) caught eight of nine targets for 53 yards and added a 13-yard rush in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons.
items.s: Flowers led the Ravens in catches and targets from backup QB Tyler Huntley while finishing nine receiving yards short of Rashod Bateman's team-leading total as the Ravens escaped with a road win Sunday night despite the absence of starting QB Lamar Jackson (ankle). Jackson reportedly has a chance to return as soon as Week 6 in Cleveland, but Flowers showed he can still be reasonably productive with Huntley throwing him passes. Flowers also took a two-yard sack on a trick play and had a would-be 26-yard catch negated on Baltimore's final drive of regulation because the Ravens instead accepted…

items.h: Flowers (foot) is listed as active for Sunday's game in Atlanta.
items.s: Flowers endured practice restrictions during Week 5 prep, only this week he was dealing with a foot injury as opposed to the hamstring issue that had plagued him since the season opener. Despite Flowers entering the weekend as questionable to play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Sunday morning that the wide receiver was slated to suit up. Now that that's been confirmed, Flowers may have less sway in fantasy terms with QB Tyler Huntley directing the offense instead of Lamar Jackson (ankle), the latter of whom is inactive.

items.h: Flowers (foot) is slated to play in Sunday night's game in Atlanta, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: Flowers swapped out his previous hamstring injury for a foot issue this week, which limited him Wednesday through Friday and left him questionable for Sunday. His status for Week 5 will be confirmed approximately 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff, and if he suits up, he'll be the preferred No. 1 pass catcher for QB Tyler Huntley, who is subbing in for an absent Lamar Jackson (ankle). That may result in a reduced target count for Flowers if the Ravens lean more on the run, but he's still put together an 18-352-2 line on 22 targets through parts of three contests this season.

items.h: Flowers (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against the Falcons.
items.s: With Flowers having been limited in practice throughout the week due to the foot issue, his status remains up in the air heading into Sunday night. He's been playing through injuries all season up to this point and could be looking at another muted workload in Atlanta. If Flowers can't play, WR Rashod Bateman and TE Mark Andrews will be Tyler Huntley's top targets.

items.h: Flowers (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday night's game at Atlanta, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
items.s: Flowers is no longer listed with a hamstring injury, instead having his practice participation limited (Wednesday through Friday) due to a foot issue. There hasn't been much to suggest it's a serious concern, but fantasy managers will still want to keep one eye on the situation this weekend ahead of an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff for the Ravens and Falcons. Quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) didn't practice this week and has been ruled out, leaving Tyler Huntley to direct Baltimore's offense.

items.h: Flowers (foot) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.s: It was the second straight limited practice for Flowers, who is now working through a foot injury in advance of Week 5. Flowers has been dynamic when on the field this year with 18 grabs for 352 yards and two touchdowns, but he's been limited to just 88 snaps across three games. Look for Flowers' status to gain more clarity Friday when the final injury report of the week is posted.

items.h: Flowers was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury.
items.s: While he was managing a hamstring strain, Flowers sat out the Ravens' Week 2 loss to the Saints and had his practice activity limited the following two weeks, but he's tending to a new injury in Week 5. The wideout was able to get some work in during Wednesday's session, but it didn't come during the media-viewing period. The Ravens' outlook on offense is already tenuous, with Lamar Jackson's ankle injury preventing him from practicing Wednesday and threatening his availability for Sunday's game in Atlanta. Flowers still has time to ramp up to a full practice before the end of the week to…

items.h: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Flowers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
items.s: Though Flowers wasn't present on the field for the media-access portion of practice, the fourth-year wideout was apparently able to get in some work behind the scenes Wednesday. The Ravens haven't indicated that Flowers has experienced any setbacks with his hamstring since returning from a one-game absence to play in both of the previous two contests, so his limitations to begin Week 5 prep were most likely maintenance-related. Flowers still appears likely to head into Sunday's game in Atlanta without an injury designation, though his fantasy appeal may be more limited than usual with Tyler…

items.s: CeeDee Lamb and Kyren Williams came up big in Week 4, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba and D'Andre Swift had disappointing days.

items.h: Flowers caught eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans.
items.s: The fourth-year wideout didn't appear hampered by the minor hamstring issue he's been playing through, as he led the Ravens in catches, targets and receiving yards while connecting with Lamar Jackson (ankle) for a 19-yard score early in the second quarter. Jackson's day was done at halftime and he was seen in a walking boot after the game, but per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, coach Jesse Minter suggested the QB might have tried playing in the second half if it seemed necessary to preserve the win. If Tyler Huntley is under center in Week 5 against the Falcons instead of Jackson,…

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) is listed as active Sunday against the Titans.
items.s: Flowers has been tending to a hamstring injury since before halftime of the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis, but he was able to play last Sunday versus the Cowboys in Brazil, recording a 5-84-0 line on six targets on a 33 percent snap share. Despite entering this weekend as questionable, he isn't expected to be on a "pitch count" Sunday, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, meaning a full workload is on tap for the fourth-year wide receiver.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Titans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Flowers carried a questionable tag into the weekend due to a lingering hamstring issue, but he's slated to suit up in Week 4 for a second straight week. Last Sunday against the Cowboys in Brazil, he handled a 33 percent snap share and hauled in five of six targets for 84 yards, but per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, Flowers isn't expected to be on a "pitch count" this Sunday, so he appears set for a full workload.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans after being limited in Friday's practice.
items.s: After upgrading to full participation Thursday, Flowers took a step back Friday, but it's possible the Ravens just rested him some considering the addition of "rest" alongside his name on the injury report, per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com. Flowers is likely better than 50/50 to play Sunday against the Titans. He's a locked-in WR2 in fantasy with big-time upside when available.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) was a full participant at Thursday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: After being limited Wednesday, Flowers upgraded to full participation Thursday, putting him on track to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans. The speedy wideout injured his hamstring in the season opener against the Colts and sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints before returning for the Ravens' Week 3 win over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. Despite missing a game, Flowers easily leads the team with 234 receiving yards.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun reports.
items.s: Baltimore is continuing to exercise caution with its star receiver, who is working his way back to 100 percent from a hamstring injury. Flowers was effective in his return Sunday but logged only 21 (33 percent) offensive snaps. He didn't aggravate the injury Sunday, though his practice reps remain limited for now.

items.h: Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that he expects Flowers to carry a full workload in Week 4 against the Titans on Sunday, Clifton Brown of the Ravens' official site reports.
items.s: Flowers had his workload limited during Sunday's 34-31 win against the Cowboys in Brazil. Despite playing only 21 snaps on offense, the fourth-year wide receiver finished with five catches on six targets for 84 yards to lead Ravens pass catchers in all three categories. Flowers will be Lamar Jackson's favorite target heading into Week 4 against a Titans defense that ranks eighth in the league in passing yards allowed per game (189.0).

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) caught five of six targets for 84 yards and added a 20-yard rush in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
items.s: Flowers led the Ravens in catches, targets and receiving yards in his return following a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. His most consequential catch was a 27-yard reception on the game's penultimate play, which set up Tyler Loop's game-winning 56-yard field goal. Per Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner, Flowers knew for a while that he would be suiting up Sunday, but he was limited in practice due to concerns about the quality of the field in Rio de Janeiro. Flowers has seemingly put the injury behind him heading into a Week 4 home game against the Titans.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: Flowers' active status is a bit of a surprise considering he's logged just one limited practice since suffering a hamstring injury in the first half of a Week 1 win at Indianapolis. On top of that, the field conditions in Brazil appear to be less than ideal, but it won't stop the Ravens from making him available to handle snaps Sunday. How many plays that may translate to remains to be seen, but Flowers and Rashod Bateman presumably will be the top wide receivers at the disposal of QB Lamar Jackson.

items.h: The Ravens continue to view Flowers (hamstring) as a game-time decision leading up to Sunday's tilt with the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, and the wide receiver is expected to be limited to "somewhere in the realm of 20…
items.s: After turning in a limited practice Friday, Flowers went through a pregame workout Sunday and appeared to be moving around well while testing out both his left hamstring and the soggy field conditions in Brazil. The Ravens are still contemplating whether to make Flowers available for the Week 3 contest, with an official call on his status expected to arrive when the team releases its inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Even if Flowers gets clearance to play, he looks like he could handle well under a full workload, making him a less appealing fantasy option than he…

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) "looked good" during a pregame workout, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, and the Ravens are still mulling whether he'll play, Adam Schefter of…
items.s: The field conditions in Brazil are a major factor in the Ravens' decision regarding the status of Flowers, who is nursing a hamstring injury and sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints. He remained sidelined for the Ravens' first two Week 3 practices back in the United States before making the trip to Brazil and turning in a limited practice Friday. Flowers seemingly responded well both to that practice and during his pregame work, but he still looks to be a true game-time call leading up to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Even if Flowers gains clearance to play, the Ravens could manage his snaps to…

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) will participate in a pregame workout to determine his status for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, but the Ravens don't appear as if they expect him to play, Adam Schefter of…
items.s: Both Schefter and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network are calling Flowers a "true pregame decision," but the field conditions in Brazil ultimately appear to be a factor in whether or not the wide receiver will be cleared for game action, according to Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. Such a call won't be made by Baltimore until about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, but if Flowers ends up missing a second game in a row, Rashod Bateman will serve as the team's No. 1 wideout.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) is expected to "test his injury" prior to Sunday's game against the Cowboys, and if he suits up he "will likely be on a pitch count," Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Flowers was limited on Friday's injury report and given a questionable designation for Week 3, so the door is open for him to take the field Sunday in Brazil. However, it appears a final call on his availability will not be made until the Ravens release their inactives 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, and even if Flowers is active he may not handle a full complement of snaps. Rashod Bateman would be the favorite to pick up the slack if Flowers is limited or unavailable altogether.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Brazil.
items.s: Flowers upgraded to limited practice participation Friday after sitting out every other session the past two weeks. It's unclear if he has a real chance to play, or if the Ravens are just trying to create that impression, so fantasy managers will need to stay tuned as the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff approaches Sunday. It'll be a tricky situation if Flowers comes down to a game-time call, but there are at least three other games with late-afternoon kickoffs, plus SNF and MNF. Flowers' teammate Rashod Bateman is one of the better replacement options after putting up 88 yards and a TD in Flowers'…

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) took part in individual drills at Friday's practice, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
items.s: This is the first sign of progress in Flowers' recovery from the hamstring injury that he suffered in the first half of the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis. Even if he goes down as a limited participant, though, he likely will be listed as questionable, at best, ahead of Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro.

items.h: The Ravens listed Flowers (hamstring) as a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: As anticipated after he was spotted working out off to the side during the media-access portion of practice, Flowers went down as a non-participant for the second consecutive day. The wideout hasn't practiced in any fashion since tweaking his hamstring in the Ravens' season-opening win over the Colts, and he could be trending toward missing a second straight game this Sunday against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. The Ravens were scheduled to fly to Brazil on Thursday, and, per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, Flowers made the trip, so it seems as if he at least has a chance to play Week 3.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) isn't practicing Thursday, though he worked out off to the side prior to practice, Kyle Goon of The Baltimore Banner reports.
items.s: Flowers has yet to resume officially participating in practice since sustaining a hamstring injury during Baltimore's season-opening win over the Colts. The speedy wide receiver sat out the Week 2 loss to the Saints and is in danger of missing a second consecutive game Sunday against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. Flowers would likely need to practice in at least some capacity Friday to have a chance to play Sunday.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) isn't participating in Wednesday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: On Monday, head coach Jesse Minter said that Flowers had a "good shot" at playing in Sunday's game against the Cowboys in Brazil, after the star wideout missed the Ravens' Week 2 loss to the Saints due to the hamstring injury. However, with Flowers opening Week 3 prep as a spectator, his availability to return to action this Sunday now appears to be more uncertain. If Flowers ends up missing a second straight game, Rashod Bateman would be line for another turn as the Ravens' No. 1 receiver.

items.h: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Flowers (hamstring) has a "good shot" to play Week 3 in Dallas, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
items.s: Listed as doubtful heading into this past Sunday's game against the Saints, Flowers was ultimately inactive for the Ravens' 24-17 loss. The team remains hopeful that Flowers' absence will be contained to just one game, and the wideout supported that optimism by returning to practice this past Friday as a limited participant. Baltimore will kick off its Week 3 prep Wednesday, and if Flowers upgrades to full practice participation that day, it would clear up any concern about his status heading into the matchup with the Cowboys.

items.h: Flowers (hamstring) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Saints.
items.s: Typically, players listed as doubtful on final injury reports of the week are inactive on game days, but the Ravens got ahead of the issue and deemed Flowers unable to play one day prior. He thus will miss at least one contest as a result of the hamstring issue he suffered in Week 1, and Baltimore will roll with a receiving corps of Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester in the meantime.
